newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BALDWIN BESTS MUSSINA AS CHISOX BLANK BALTIMORE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BALDWIN BESTS MUSSINA AS CHISOX BLANK BALTIMORE.

text.p: James Baldwin and two relievers combined on a three-hitter and Albert Belle supplied some long ball as the Chicago White Sox snapped a four-game skid with a 3-0 victory over the slumping Baltimore Orioles.
Baldwin (7-9), who has won four of his last five decisions, scattered two hits and three walks in seven-plus innings and atoned for a 10-2 loss to the Orioles last month.
"(Catcher Jorge) Fabregas called a great game," said Baldwin after outduelling Mike Mussina. "When you go up there against Mussina, it boosts you up."
Roberto Hernandez worked the ninth for his 24th save.
Baltimore ace Mussina (10-4) dropped his second straight start, giving up two runs and seven hits with two walks and eight strikeouts in eight innings.
"It doesn't really matter how good I throw if I give up two runs and he gives up none," said Mussina.
The Orioles, whose 57-36 mark is best in the American League, have lost three straight and nine of their last 11.

"We're just not doing things we were early in the season," said Orioles manager Davey Johnson. "I'm glad it's happening this time of the year instead of late. We'll right ourselves soon, but it's trying on everybody."

Chicago broke a scoreless tie in the seventh when Mussina wild-pitched a run in with two out and the bases loaded. Belle belted his 21st homer with two out in the eighth and Norberto Martin singled in a run off closer Randy Myers in the ninth.

In Seattle, Randy Johnson became the second 13-game winner in the American League as Edgar Martinez and Ken Griffey Jr. each had two RBI to boost the Mariners past the nose-diving Kansas City Royals 5-4.
Johnson (13-2) struck out 16 while allowing nine hits to join Toronto's Roger Clemens as a 13-game winner.
"I scuffled all night, even though I felt good all night," said Johnson. "I don't grade my performance I'm just happy that I'm in here and we won."

"Our boys battled hard and they accepted the challenge (of facing Johnson)," said manager Tony Muser, after the Royals lost for the 16th time in 17 games. "They went after him and we made a ball game of it. It hurts to lose."
Kansas City held a 3-2 lead before the Mariners scored three times in the bottom of the fourth in an outburst capped by a Griffey's two-run single.
In Cleveland, Tim Wakefield threw a six-hitter for his first shutout in more than two years and Jeff Frye drove in three runs as the Boston Red Sox blanked the Indians 7-0.
Wakefield (4-10) scattered five singles and a double to post his second consecutive complete game.
"Tim was awesome," said Frye. "His ball must of been moving, because they have some great hitters and they were taking some bad swings."
In Milwaukee, Jeromy Burnitz hit a three-run homer off former teammate Dwight Gooden to snap a fifth-inning tie and lift the Brewers to a 6-4 victory over the New York Yankees.
Burnitz and Gooden were teammates on the 1993-94 Mets.

"Doc, his fastball is not what it used to be," Burnitz said. "He's still got decent breaking stuff. I didn't have to key in on one pitch. I was just looking for the ball, cause he doesn't throw anything overpowering anymore. I got a good curveball to hit."
Milwaukee's Jeff D'Amico (8-4) took the win. Mike Fetters pitched 1 2/3 innings for his first save since last September.

At Texas, Willie Blair pitched 6 1/3 solid innings for his fourth straight win and Bob Higginson and Brian Hunter each drove in two runs as the Detroit Tigers held on for a 5-4 victory over the Texas Rangers.
Blair (8-4) established a career high with his eighth win, as the Tigers backed him with two runs in the third and fourth innings and a single tally in the sixth.
Bobby Witt (10-5) took the loss.

In Anaheim, Woody Williams combined with two relievers on a seven-hitter and Benito Santiago homered for the first time in more than two months as the Toronto Blue Jays edged the Anaheim Angels 2-1, ending their 10-game winning streak.
Williams (5-8) allowed one run and seven hits in 6 2/3.
Rookie Kelvim Escobar, 21, continued to excel out of the bullpen, striking out two in a hitless ninth for his second save. He has yet to allow a run in 10 1/3 innings.
"He's been flawless," Toronto manager Cito Gaston said.

In Oakland, LaTroy Hawkins pitched eight-plus innings to snap a personal five-game losing streak and Pat Meares had three hits and two RBI to lead the Minnesota Twins to a 7-3 win over the Oakland Athletics.
Hawkins (2-5) allowed three runs and eight hits.
"We knew he had a good arm," Oakland manager Art Howe said about Hawkins. "We hit the ball hard with men on base but he was lucky enough to have them hit at somebody."
